children: Saudi Arabia reported to OPEC on Thursday that its crude oil production plunged in August to the lowest since 1990, as renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran as well as threats against shipping by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen squeezed Saudi export routes.
The kingdom's output tumbled by 1.9M bbl/day to 6.23M bbl/day in August, its lowest monthly figure this year and 23% lower than in July, according to a report published by the cartel.

The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" on Saudi ports at the end of July, deterring ship operators from the area and forcing a reduction in the kingdom's crude exports to 3.1M bbl/day in August from 5.1M bbl/day in July, its lowest export level since at least 2013, according to Kpler.

Curtailed Red Sea exports likely will continue as the Houthis have stepped up their strikes on Saudi oil this week, hitting multiple energy facilities in a wave of attacks, and reportedly seized control of Yemen's port city of Mocha on Thursday, posing a ​further threat to global energy supplies through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, one of the world's most important shipping routes.
Saudi Arabia had relied on the Red Sea shipping route since ​the Iran conflict effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.
Crude oil futures jumped another ~3% on Thursday after this week's spike in attacks on shipping in the Middle East sparked trader concerns about supply disruptions.

title: Saudi Arabia says its crude oil production plunged last month to lowest since 1990
